mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns do not decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises and employment (PAYEMS) falls simultaneously, it indicates a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but returns are positive, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates monetary easing, boosting equity markets and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is low but returns aren't higher, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL) erodes purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If inflation is high but returns are positive, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth (INDPRO) above 2% signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If growth exceeds 2% but returns don't rise, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: If both increase but returns don't rise, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high but returns don't drop, the hypothesis is falsified.
